notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. 233 entries, 184 distinct names, and 36 rows literally called `nop` -- padding between the blocks, one per replayer, so a later version can add a keyword without moving anybody's ids. THIRTEEN REPLAYERS IN ONE LIBRARY, each with the same shape of load/play/stop/cont/volume/song pos/patt pos/vu: `dmed` (MED), `omed` (OctaMED), `omix` (OctaMIX, with a 14-bit mode), `sid`, `ptm` (ProTracker, and the only one with a CIA speed), `thx`, `p61`, `fc13`, `fc14`, `smon` (SoundMon), `sfx13`, `db` (DigiBooster, with a mixer and a boost rate), `tfmx`, `s3m` and `xm`, plus a `dme sam *` sampler. It shares four `p61 *` names with the registered P61 extension and all six `thx *` names with THX 0.6, and shares NOT ONE ID with either -- which is what made the cataloguer score on ids rather than names. THE ARCHIVE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE EXTENSION: libs/ holds ELEVEN FORMAT REPLAYERS as separate Amiga libraries, all dated 3 Nov 1997 -- DME_FastTracker (XM, 26,324 bytes), DME_OctaMix (24,140), DME_Med (15,448), DME_ScreamTracker (S3M, 13,844), DME_OctaMed (13,244), DME_DigiBooster (13,080), DME_TFMX (9,544), DME_FC1.3 (6,460), DME_FC1.4 (6,212), DME_SoundMon2.0 (4,520) and DME_SoundFX1.3 (3,476). This port has protracker.ts and p61.ts and nothing else, so that is the reading material for every other tracker format in the corpus whether or not this row is ever ported. Note which formats have EXAMPLES but no library: Protracker, P61, PlaySid and THX are either built in or expected from LIBS: -- settle it from this library's own OpenLibrary calls, not from the file list. Its error strings ("Can't load DME_OctaMix.library V2.0 or higher") show the loading is per-format and versioned.
